---
params:
  x:
  tab_title:
  type:
  meta: !r NULL
  cohort: !r NULL
title: "Strukturtabelle `r params$tab_title`"
subtitle: "`r paste0(if(params$type == 'dq') 'nach Mitteldurchmesser-Klassen' else 'nach Altersklassen', if (identical(params$cohort, 'mainstand')) ', Hauptbestand' else if (identical(params$cohort, 'alllayers')) ', Alle Schichten' else paste0(', Benutzerdefinierte Auswahl: ', params$cohort))`"
classoption:
  - a4paper
geometry:
  - portrait
  - "left=0.7cm,right=0.7cm,top=1cm,bottom=1.2cm"
fontsize: 10pt
header-includes:
  - \renewcommand{\maketitle}{}
  - \usepackage{array}
  # adjustbox scales the title on the title page; siunitx used to be loaded
  # here for "S" columns that were never actually applied (see the width
  # section in the table chunk).
  - \usepackage{adjustbox}
---
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "asis"}

# https://haozhu233.github.io/kableExtra/awesome_table_in_html.html
# https://www.pipinghotdata.com/posts/2022-01-24-report-ready-pdf-tables-with-rmarkdown-knitr-kableextra-and-latex/

oo <- options(knitr.kable.NA = "", fe_spec_lang = "ger")

# Take the table from params, not from the calling frame. rmarkdown::render()
# evaluates in the caller's environment, so a bare `x` happened to resolve to
# the local variable of output_structure_table_pdf() - which only works as long
# as that argument keeps its name. Everything below works on this local copy.
x <- params$x

x <- x |> dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$variable != "tot_area_class")

class_col <- if (params$type == "age") "age_class" else "d_q_class"

# 1. The confidence interval is shown in the "Gesamt" column only. Per dbh
# class it is computed over a handful of inventory points - ex3 produces 530 %
# and 754 % - and such a figure says nothing except that the subgroup is too
# small to say anything. The Gesamt cell carries the properly aggregated
# class-wise interval (the very one the base table prints), so the row keeps
# its meaning without the noise.
class_cols <- setdiff(names(x), c("species_group", class_col, "variable", "total"))
x[x$variable == "conf_95_per", class_cols] <- NA

# 2. Translate variable names. The wording follows output_base_table_template_
# ger.Rmd literally wherever the two tables show the same quantity, so a reader
# moving between them meets the same labels.
x <- x |>
  dplyr::mutate(variable = dplyr::recode(.data$variable,
    # main-stand (per-ha) variables
    area_ha      = "Fl. ideell (ha)",
    n_ha         = "N (/ha)",
    g_m2_ha      = "G (m²/ha)",
    v_hub_m3_ha  = "V (m³/ha)",
    conf_95_per  = "95%-VB (± %)",
    # non-main-stand (aggregate) variables
    v_hub_m3     = "V (m³)",
    g_m2         = "G (m²)",
    n            = "N",
    d_q_cm       = "dg (cm)",
    h_q_m        = "hg (m)",
    n_plot       = "Anz. Pkte.",
    # Row content is unchanged (the standing-volume distribution across the dbh
    # classes, row-normalised, verified against BaySF's own report); only the
    # label moves into the base table's naming scheme, where a share row says
    # which quantity is shared out and across what.
    pct_anteil_v = "V-Ant. Bhd-Kl. (%)"
  ))

# 2a. The area share needs a block-dependent label, exactly as in the base
# table, because the one variable carries two meanings. Inside a species block
# it is that species group's share of the class' ideal area (the Gesamt cell is
# the species' share of the class). In the cross-species block there is no
# species left to distinguish, so the same figure becomes the dbh class' share
# of its own class' ideal area - which is why that block's Gesamt cell reads
# 100 % throughout.
x <- x |>
  dplyr::mutate(variable = dplyr::case_when(
    .data$variable != "per_species" ~ .data$variable,
    is.na(.data$species_group)      ~ "Fl.-Ant. Bhd-Kl. (%)",
    TRUE                            ~ "Fl.-Ant. Artgr. (%)"
  ))

# 2b. Row order, as in the base table: an annotation row sits directly under
# the quantity it belongs to, and "Anz. Pkte." always comes last. Rows a
# variant does not have (the area / per-ha rows exist only in the main-stand
# variant) are simply skipped.
.var_order <- c("V (m³)", "95%-VB (± %)", "V-Ant. Bhd-Kl. (%)",
                "G (m²)", "N", "dg (cm)", "hg (m)",
                "Fl. ideell (ha)", "Fl.-Ant. Artgr. (%)", "Fl.-Ant. Bhd-Kl. (%)",
                "V (m³/ha)", "G (m²/ha)", "N (/ha)",
                "Anz. Pkte.")
#
# Row groups are ordered explicitly rather than by the class factor alone: the
# real classes come first in ascending order, then the trees without a class
# ("k. A.", whose level is NA and which dplyr would otherwise sort last of
# all), and the pooling group ("Summe" -> "Alle Klassen") closes the block.
x <- x |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    variable = factor(.data$variable, levels = .var_order, ordered = TRUE),
    .class_rank = dplyr::case_when(
      as.character(.data[[class_col]]) == "Summe" ~ 3L,
      is.na(.data[[class_col]])                   ~ 2L,
      TRUE                                        ~ 1L
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(is.na(.data$species_group), .data$species_group,
                 .data$.class_rank, .data[[class_col]], .data$variable) |>
  dplyr::mutate(variable = as.character(.data$variable)) |>
  dplyr::select(-".class_rank")

# 3. dg and hg are blanked in exactly one place per species: where the "Alle
# Klassen" row group meets the "Gesamt" column. Everywhere else they stay.
# Within a single class the Gesamt column pools nothing but the dbh classes,
# which is a meaningful basal-area mean tree - and precisely the value the base
# table prints for that class. Only the trailing row group pools every class,
# so that one cell is the counterpart of the base table's "Gesamt" column,
# blanked there for the same reason: a single dg spanning thicket to old timber
# describes no real stand. Cells are set to NA rather than rows dropped
# (knitr.kable.NA = ""), so the per-class values are untouched.
x$total[as.character(x[[class_col]]) == "Summe" &
          x$variable %in% c("dg (cm)", "hg (m)")] <- NA

# 4. Pre-format every numeric cell, German conventions: decimal comma and
# thousands separated by a space (unambiguous to German and English readers
# alike, unlike a thousands dot). V, G, N and the point counts are whole
# numbers; everything else keeps one decimal.
#
# The former "Tsd." rescaling is gone. Dividing V, G and N by 1000 and printing
# three decimals showed the same information - resolution down to the single
# cubic metre - in a form nobody can read at a glance: ex3 rendered V as 0,000
# / 0,041 / 0,110 and N as 78,214. Whole numbers with a thin thousands space
# say the same thing plainly, and they degrade gracefully for small
# enterprises, which the rescaling did not.
fmt_de <- function(v, digits) {
  formatC(v, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = " ", decimal.mark = ",")
}
int_rows   <- c("V (m³)", "G (m²)", "N", "Anz. Pkte.")
is_int_row <- x$variable %in% int_rows
for (cn in names(x)[vapply(x, is.numeric, logical(1))]) {
  x[[cn]] <- dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(x[[cn]]) ~ NA_character_,
    is_int_row     ~ fmt_de(round(x[[cn]]), 0),
    TRUE           ~ fmt_de(x[[cn]], 1)
  )
}

# 5. Open top class: "(60,999]" -> ">60" (999 is the sentinel upper break from
# pulled_methods.R). This affects both axes of this table - the dbh classes in
# the column headers and the age/dq classes in the row-group headings - so it
# is applied to the column names here and to the group labels below.
open_class <- function(s) sub("^\\(([0-9]+),999\\]$", ">\\1", s)
names(x) <- open_class(names(x))

# Trees without an age form a class whose level is NA; it becomes the "k. A."
# row group (see the loop). Recorded here, while the class column is still
# around, because the notes on the title page only mention it when it is there.
has_no_class_group <- any(is.na(x[[class_col]]))
# Name the leftover row-label column after the class it groups (Altersklasse/
# Dg-Klasse) rather than a generic "Kennzahl" - it's the only place left that
# tells the reader what the sub-headings below it actually are.
label_col <- if (params$type == "age") "Altersklasse" else "Dg-Klasse"

# Species order: real species first (original order), the cross-species block
# (NA species_group) forced last. Three different things used to be called
# "Summe" in this table; they are now told apart by name, following the base
# table: the cross-species page is "Alle Artgruppen", the total column is
# "Gesamt" (see the rename below), and the trailing row group of each page -
# the one pooling every class - is "Alle Klassen".
sp_order_dat <- x |>
  dplyr::distinct(species_group) |>
  dplyr::arrange(is.na(species_group), species_group)
sp_keys   <- sp_order_dat$species_group
sp_labels <- format(sp_keys)
sp_labels[is.na(sp_keys)] <- "Alle Artgruppen"

# Escape the handful of LaTeX-special characters that could in principle show
# up in a species label, before dropping it into raw LaTeX below.
latex_escape <- function(s) gsub("([&_%$#{}])", "\\\\\\1", s)

# Keep a class block together on one page. Same mechanism as the base table and
# the increment tables: pack_rows starts every group with a line
# "\addlinespace[0.3em]", and a longtable row ending in "\\" allows a page break
# after it while "\\*" forbids one. So every breakable row terminator becomes
# "\\*", except the one right before the next group boundary - breaks then
# happen between blocks, never inside one. A block is a good page-and-a-bit
# shorter than a page, so nothing gets stranded.
#
# This only works together with pack_rows(hline_before = TRUE): a rule below
# the heading would be a break opportunity that no penalty can close, because
# longtable offers a break at a rule deliberately and offers it before anything
# we could append. See the pack_rows call.
no_break_within_groups <- function(tex, n_col) {
  lines <- strsplit(tex, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  is_boundary <- trimws(lines) == "\\addlinespace[0.3em]"
  n <- length(lines)
  out <- character(0)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    ln <- lines[i]
    if (endsWith(ln, "\\\\") && !endsWith(ln, "\\\\*")) {
      j <- i + 1L
      while (j <= n && trimws(lines[j]) == "") j <- j + 1L
      next_boundary <- j <= n && is_boundary[j]
      next_end      <- j <= n && grepl("end{longtable}", lines[j], fixed = TRUE)
      if (!next_boundary && !next_end) ln <- paste0(ln, "*")
    }
    out <- c(out, ln)
  }
  paste(out, collapse = "\n")
}

# Set the area / per-hectare rows off visually: a rule above the first of them
# and one below the last, so everything resting on the ideal species areas is
# bracketed off from the rest. Taken over from the base table, including the
# reasoning for the rule type: deliberately \cmidrule and not \midrule, because
# \midrule spans the full tabular width like the class separators, whereas
# \cmidrule(lr){1-n} covers just the labels and the numbers and is trimmed at
# both ends, so it reads as a subdivision inside a block rather than as another
# block boundary. Only the main-stand variant carries these rows at all; here
# they occur once per class block, so every occurrence gets its pair.
bracket_block <- function(tex, first_row, last_row, n_col) {
  lines <- strsplit(tex, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  # Trimmed to the printed matter rather than to the columns: on the left by
  # the cell padding plus the indent pack_rows puts in front of every row
  # label, so the rule starts exactly under the first letter of the variable
  # names; on the right by the cell padding alone, so it ends flush with the
  # right edge of the numbers.
  rule  <- sprintf(
    "\\cmidrule(l{\\dimexpr\\tabcolsep+1em\\relax}r{\\tabcolsep}){1-%d}", n_col)
  out   <- character(0)
  for (ln in lines) {
    if (grepl(first_row, ln, fixed = TRUE)) out <- c(out, rule)
    out <- c(out, ln)
    if (grepl(last_row, ln, fixed = TRUE))  out <- c(out, rule)
  }
  paste(out, collapse = "\n")
}

# 6. Fit the table to the text width, with the same self-measuring mechanism as
# the base table. Neither the number of dbh classes nor the magnitude of the
# numbers is fixed, so no constant can be right for every inventory; the levers
# are the type size and the inter-column padding, and both are derived from the
# content that is actually there.
#
# The width of a column is estimated from its widest entry, charging 0.5 em per
# digit or letter and 0.3 em for spaces and punctuation. Padding is given up
# before type size, because tighter columns are far less noticeable than
# smaller print.
#
# Measured over the whole table at once, not per species: every page carries
# the same columns, so the widest content anywhere decides, and one type size
# holds for the entire document instead of jumping from page to page.
#
# This replaces a block that rewrote the numeric columns to siunitx "S"
# columns. That block never did anything: it searched the tabular preamble for
# the literal "{lrr...r}", but column_spec() had already turned the preamble
# into "{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{1.9cm}rr...r}", so the sub() silently
# found nothing. The columns have always been plain right-aligned - which is
# also all that "S" would have delivered, since \sisetup sets
# parse-numbers=false. siunitx is therefore no longer loaded.
page_width_cm <- 21.0   # a4paper (classoption in the YAML header)
margin_cm     <- 0.7    # keep in sync with the geometry setting above
text_width_pt <- (page_width_cm - 2 * margin_cm) / 2.54 * 72.27

# Character widths come from the font, not from a rule of thumb. Computer
# Modern is optically sized: at small type sizes every glyph is proportionally
# wider, so the familiar "half an em per character" - about right at 10 pt - is
# far too narrow down here, and the error grows with the length of the numbers.
# Measured with pdflatex (\settowidth at each candidate size), a digit is
#   5 pt: 0.680 em   6 pt: 0.611 em   7 pt: 0.569 em   8 pt: 0.531 em
# which in points is what the table below holds. The remaining glyph classes
# keep an almost constant ratio to the digit across these sizes, so they are
# expressed as multiples of it. All of this is metric of the typeface - it
# holds for every table this template ever renders and depends on no data.
digit_pt <- c("5" = 0.680 * 5, "6" = 0.611 * 6,
              "7" = 0.569 * 7, "8" = 0.531 * 8)

char_units <- function(chs) {
  u <- rep(1.00, length(chs))               # digits and lowercase letters
  u[chs == " "]                          <- 0.70
  u[chs %in% c(",", ".")]                <- 0.60
  u[chs %in% c("(", ")", "[", "]", "-", "/")] <- 0.80
  u[chs == "%"]                          <- 1.65
  u[chs %in% LETTERS]                    <- 1.45
  u
}

str_width_units <- function(s) {
  s <- s[!is.na(s)]
  if (length(s) == 0) return(0)
  max(vapply(strsplit(s, "", fixed = TRUE),
             function(chs) sum(char_units(chs)), numeric(1)))
}

# The row-label column carries the variable names, the class column is dropped
# before rendering, and species_group never reaches the table.
measured   <- x |> dplyr::select(-dplyr::all_of(c("species_group", class_col)))
n_tbl_cols <- ncol(measured)
col_units <- vapply(seq_along(measured), function(j) {
  max(str_width_units(as.character(measured[[j]])),
      str_width_units(names(measured)[j]))
}, numeric(1))

# A structure table is wide by nature - thirteen dbh classes plus a total
# column - so it starts one step below the base table's ladder. Together with
# the wider page margin this keeps a comfortable distance to the paper edge
# instead of filling it out to the last point.
font_sizes <- c(7, 6, 5)
colseps    <- c(6, 4, 3, 2)

# What is still not modelled: the width of the booktabs rules, and rounding in
# the glyph factors. Both are small and neither grows with the data, so a
# narrow margin suffices - unlike before, when the whole character model was
# wrong and the shortfall grew with the size of the numbers.
width_budget_pt <- 0.96 * text_width_pt

# Fallback if even the smallest combination is too wide: use it anyway, so the
# table comes out as narrow as this mechanism can make it.
fit   <- list(font_size = min(font_sizes), colsep = min(colseps))
found <- FALSE
for (fs in font_sizes) {
  # pack_rows indents the label of every data row by 1 em, which is exactly the
  # type size in points - a known quantity, so it is charged rather than
  # absorbed into the margin.
  content_pt <- sum(col_units) * digit_pt[[as.character(fs)]] + fs
  for (cs in colseps) {
    if (content_pt + 2 * cs * n_tbl_cols <= width_budget_pt) {
      fit   <- list(font_size = fs, colsep = cs)
      found <- TRUE
      break
    }
  }
  if (found) break
}

# 7. Title page. Pandoc's own \maketitle is suppressed (header-includes), so
# title, subtitle and meta line are built by hand here, centred on a page of
# their own, and the data start fresh on page 2 - one species per page after
# that. The page is emitted from this chunk rather than from an earlier one
# because the explanatory notes below need the labels the steps above produce.
subtitle_txt <- paste0(
  if (params$type == "dq") "nach Mitteldurchmesser-Klassen" else "nach Altersklassen",
  if (identical(params$cohort, "mainstand")) ", Hauptbestand"
  else if (identical(params$cohort, "alllayers")) ", Alle Schichten"
  else paste0(", Benutzerdefinierte Auswahl: ", latex_escape(params$cohort))
)

cat("\\begin{center}\n\\vspace*{\\fill}\n")
cat("\\adjustbox{max width=0.95\\linewidth}{\\Huge\\textbf{Strukturtabelle ",
    latex_escape(params$tab_title), "}}\\\\[1em]\n", sep = "")
cat("{\\Large ", subtitle_txt, "}\\\\[2em]\n", sep = "")

if (!is.null(params$meta)) {
  m <- params$meta
  # Thousands separated by a space, not a dot, as in the base table: "15 575"
  # reads the same to German and English readers, whereas "15.575" looks like a
  # decimal number.
  fmt_ha <- function(v) format(round(v), big.mark = " ", decimal.mark = ",",
                                scientific = FALSE)
  parts <- character(0)
  if (!is.null(m$year))    parts <- c(parts, paste0("\\textbf{Inventurjahr:} ",      as.integer(m$year)))
  if (!is.null(m$area_ha)) parts <- c(parts, paste0("\\textbf{Gesamtfl\\\"ache:} ", fmt_ha(m$area_ha), " ha"))
  if (!is.null(m$n_plots)) parts <- c(parts, paste0("\\textbf{Inventurpunkte:} ",   as.integer(m$n_plots)))
  if (length(parts) > 0)
    cat("{\\large ", paste(parts, collapse = " \\qquad "), "}\n", sep = "")
}

cat("\\vspace*{\\fill}\n\\end{center}\n")

# 7a. Explanatory notes, taken over from the base table so both table families
# explain the same quantity in the same words. They sit on the title page here
# rather than under the table, because the table runs over many pages and there
# is no single "under it" any more. The cohort caveat is the first note, which
# is what makes the separate disclaimer footnote (and the asterisk in the
# subtitle it referred to) unnecessary.
#
# Which notes appear depends on the rows this variant actually carries, so
# nothing is explained that is not shown.
has <- function(v) v %in% unique(x$variable)
# "%" starts a comment in LaTeX and this block is emitted as raw LaTeX.
esc <- function(s) gsub("%", "\\\\%", s)

notes <- character(0)
if (identical(params$cohort, "mainstand")) {
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "Diese Tabelle umfasst nur den Hauptbestand, nicht das gesamte erfasste ",
    "Inventurkollektiv. Nur f\\\"ur den Hauptbestand lassen sich ideelle ",
    "Baumarten-Anteilsfl\\\"achen und darauf bezogene Hektarwerte berechnen. Die ",
    "Berechnung solcher ideellen Anteilsfl\\\"achen ist aus methodischer Sicht ",
    "allerdings problematisch; darauf bezogene Werte sind stets mit Vorsicht zu ",
    "interpretieren."))
} else if (identical(params$cohort, "alllayers")) {
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "Diese Tabelle beinhaltet die Werte aller Bestandesschichten. Sie umfasst ",
    "daher das gesamte Holzvolumen des Betriebes, erlaubt aber nicht die ",
    "Berechnung von ideellen Fl\\\"achenanteilen und daher auch nicht die Angabe ",
    "von darauf bezogenen Per-Hektar-Werten."))
}
notes <- c(notes, paste0(
  "Alle Volumenangaben verstehen sich als Erntefestmeter ohne Rinde (Efm o.R.)."))
notes <- c(notes, paste0(
  "Aufbau: je Artgruppe eine Seite, darauf je Klasse ein Block; die letzte ",
  "Seite \"Alle Artgruppen\" fasst \\\"uber alle Artgruppen zusammen. Der ",
  "abschlie\\ss{}ende Block \"Alle Klassen\" b\\\"undelt alle Klassen der jeweiligen ",
  "Seite, die Spalte \"Gesamt\" alle Bhd-Klassen der jeweiligen Zeile."))
notes <- c(notes, paste0(
  "Bhd-Klassen ohne B\\\"aume werden als leere Spalte gezeigt, damit die ",
  "Klassenachse vollst\\\"andig und zwischen Auswertungen vergleichbar bleibt."))
if (has_no_class_group)
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "k. A.: keine Altersangabe. Dieser Block fasst alle B\\\"aume zusammen, f\\\"ur ",
    "die kein Alter vorliegt; er bildet eine eigene Klasse und geht damit in den ",
    "Block \"Alle Klassen\" ein."))
if (has("95%-VB (± %)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "95%-VB (± %): halbe Breite des zweiseitigen 95%-Vertrauensbereichs des ",
    "Vorrats V, in Prozent von V. Der zugrundeliegende Standardfehler ist ",
    "fl\\\"achengewichtet gesch\\\"atzt. Der Wert wird nur in der Spalte \"Gesamt\" ",
    "ausgewiesen, also je Klasse: je einzelner Bhd-Klasse st\\\"utzte er sich auf ",
    "so wenige Inventurpunkte, dass er nichts aussagt."))
if (has("dg (cm)") || has("hg (m)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "dg, hg: Durchmesser bzw. H\\\"ohe des Grundfl\\\"achenmittelstamms. Im ",
    "Schnittpunkt des Blocks \"Alle Klassen\" mit der Spalte \"Gesamt\" werden sie ",
    "nicht ausgewiesen: \\\"uber alle Klassen hinweg ist die Angabe eines ",
    "Mittelstamms nicht sinnvoll."))
if (has("V-Ant. Bhd-Kl. (%)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "V-Ant. Bhd-Kl. (%): Anteil der jeweiligen Bhd-Klasse am Vorrat der Zeile. ",
    "Die Werte einer Zeile summieren sich \\\"uber alle Bhd-Klassen zu 100 %."))
if (has("Fl. ideell (ha)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "Fl. ideell (ha): ideelle Anteilsfl\\\"ache der Artgruppe; die hektarbezogenen ",
    "Werte beziehen sich auf diese Fl\\\"ache."))
if (has("Fl.-Ant. Artgr. (%)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "Fl.-Ant. Artgr. (%): Anteil der Artgruppe an der ideellen Fl\\\"ache der ",
    "jeweiligen Klasse. Die Werte einer Klasse summieren sich \\\"uber alle ",
    "Artgruppen zu 100 %."))
if (has("Fl.-Ant. Bhd-Kl. (%)"))
  notes <- c(notes, paste0(
    "Fl.-Ant. Bhd-Kl. (%): Anteil der jeweiligen Bhd-Klasse an der ideellen ",
    "Fl\\\"ache der Klasse. Die Werte einer Zeile summieren sich \\\"uber alle ",
    "Bhd-Klassen zu 100 %."))
notes <- c(notes, paste0(
  "Anz. Pkte.: Anzahl der Inventurpunkte, auf denen die jeweilige Gruppe ",
  "vertreten ist. Die Summe \\\"uber die Tabelle kann von der oben angegebenen ",
  "Gesamtzahl der Inventurpunkte abweichen, weil nicht auf jedem Inventurpunkt ",
  "B\\\"aume vorkommen, die den Auswahlkriterien dieser Tabelle entsprechen."))

# Emitted as raw LaTeX: use real environments throughout. A bare "{ ... }"
# grouping is NOT recognised as LaTeX by pandoc and would leak into the text.
#
# The notes sit in a centred minipage rather than across the full text width.
# The page margin is set narrow for the sake of the wide table, which leaves
# running text uncomfortably close to the paper edge; the minipage gives the
# notes their own, roomier measure without touching the geometry the table
# depends on.
cat("\\vfill\n\\begin{center}\\begin{minipage}{0.88\\linewidth}\n")
cat("\\begin{footnotesize}\n")
cat("\\textbf{Erl\\\"auterungen}\n")
cat("\\begin{itemize}\\setlength{\\itemsep}{0pt}\\setlength{\\parskip}{0pt}",
    "\\setlength{\\topsep}{2pt}\n", sep = "")
for (nt in notes) cat("\\item ", esc(nt), "\n", sep = "")
cat("\\end{itemize}\n\\end{footnotesize}\n")
cat("\\end{minipage}\\end{center}\n")

cat("\n\\newpage\n")

# Emitted as a plain command (no brace group), which pandoc passes through as
# raw LaTeX; the tables below are the only tabular material in the document.
cat("\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{", fit$colsep, "pt}\n", sep = "")


for (i in seq_along(sp_keys)) {
  key <- sp_keys[i]
  sp_dat <- if (is.na(key)) {
    x[is.na(x$species_group), ]
  } else {
    x[!is.na(x$species_group) & x$species_group == key, ]
  }
  sp_dat <- sp_dat |> dplyr::select(-species_group)

  # The class columns are counted by exclusion, never by the "(a,b]" spelling
  # of their names: the open top class is relabelled ">60" above, and an age
  # level of NA arrives as a column named "NA", so a spelling test would leave
  # either of them outside the spanner.
  has_total    <- "total" %in% names(sp_dat)
  n_class_cols <- ncol(sp_dat) - 2L - as.integer(has_total)

  # Age/dq class sub-heading (bold), nested within this species' own table,
  # with a rule along the row's own lower border separating it from the
  # class' data rows below (hline_after = TRUE) - simpler and more robust
  # than a decorative fill-line.
  # Trees whose age is unknown form a class whose level is NA. It is labelled
  # "k. A." - the same wording the base table uses for its no-age column, so
  # both table families read alike. Note also that pack_rows() cannot take an
  # NA group name at all ("NAs are not allowed in subscripted assignments"), so
  # without this the whole age-class structure table failed to render for any
  # inventory with incomplete ages.
  class_chr    <- as.character(sp_dat[[class_col]])
  is_summe_row <- !is.na(class_chr) & class_chr == "Summe"
  # The open top class needs the same relabelling here as in the column heads:
  # this is the second place it appears, as the heading of a row group.
  class_chr    <- open_class(class_chr)
  class_chr[is.na(class_chr)] <- "k. A."
  class_chr[is_summe_row]     <- "Alle Klassen"

  class_rle   <- rle(class_chr)
  class_index <- class_rle$lengths
  names(class_index) <- class_rle$values

  sp_dat <- sp_dat |>
    dplyr::rename(!!label_col := variable) |>
    dplyr::rename("Gesamt" = total) |>
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::all_of(class_col))

  horizontal_index <- c(1, n_class_cols, if (has_total) 1 else 0)
  names(horizontal_index) <- c(" ", "Bhd-Klassen (cm)", if (has_total) " " else NULL)

  tbl <- knitr::kable(
    sp_dat,
    booktabs    = TRUE,
    longtable   = TRUE,
    format.args = list(scientific = FALSE),
    align       = c("l", rep("r", ncol(sp_dat) - 1)),
    linesep     = ""
  ) |>
    kableExtra::add_header_above(horizontal_index) |>
    kableExtra::pack_rows(
      index        = class_index,
      # The rule sits above the block heading, not below it. Below the heading
      # it was a page-break opportunity that could not be closed: longtable
      # offers a break at a rule on purpose, and the offer comes before any
      # penalty that could follow it, so the heading kept being stranded alone
      # at the foot of a page. Above the heading the same rule falls on a block
      # boundary, which is exactly where a break is welcome anyway - and it
      # reads as a block separator, which is what it is.
      hline_after  = FALSE,
      hline_before = TRUE,
      bold         = TRUE,
      italic       = FALSE,
      indent       = TRUE
    ) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      font_size     = fit$font_size,
      latex_options = "repeat_header"
    )
  # The row-label column takes its natural width; no column_spec(width =) is
  # applied. A fixed width is a guess that has to be re-guessed whenever a
  # label changes - "V-Ant. Bhd-Kl. (%)" wrapped onto two lines in the previous
  # 1.9 cm - whereas the label set is decided by this template alone, so LaTeX
  # can size the column exactly and never wrap.

  # Order matters: forbid the breaks first, then insert the rules. The break
  # logic reads the row terminators, and a \cmidrule line has none - inserting
  # the rules first would put a non-row line between a row and the group
  # boundary that follows it, and the row would wrongly be marked unbreakable.
  tex <- no_break_within_groups(as.character(tbl), ncol(sp_dat))
  if ("Fl. ideell (ha)" %in% sp_dat[[label_col]] &&
      "N (/ha)" %in% sp_dat[[label_col]])
    tex <- bracket_block(tex, "Fl. ideell (ha) &", "N (/ha) &", ncol(sp_dat))

  # The species heading goes inside the table, as a row of its own above the
  # top rule, instead of being written above it as ordinary text. The table is
  # centred on the page, so its left edge is nowhere near the left margin, and
  # a heading set as text started well to the left of it. As a table row it
  # begins exactly where the top rule begins - "@{}" drops the cell padding
  # that would otherwise push it a little to the right. It sits before
  # \endfirsthead, so it appears once and is not repeated on continuation
  # pages.
  head_row <- sprintf("\\multicolumn{%d}{@{}l}{\\LARGE\\textbf{%s}}\\\\[0.4em]",
                      ncol(sp_dat), latex_escape(sp_labels[i]))
  tex <- sub("\\toprule", paste0(head_row, "\n\\toprule"), tex, fixed = TRUE)

  cat("\n\\bigskip\n\n")
  cat(tex, sep = "\n")
  if (i < length(sp_keys)) cat("\n\\newpage\n")
}

options(oo)
```
